verdict.rationale: Honeycomb documents instrumenting with OpenTelemetry SDKs and natively ingesting OTLP over gRPC, HTTP/protobuf, and HTTP/JSON. It states that apps already instrumented with OpenTelemetry can send OTLP directly to Honeycomb, so you can switch to it without re-instrumenting. It also offers migration paths from its proprietary Beelines and other legacy instrumentation to OpenTelemetry. missing for 10: explicit documentation that Honeycomb-bound instrumentation stays portable when leaving for another backend (e.g., Collector-based routing or multi-export), independent or hands-on corroboration of a backend switch.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can instrument once with open standards and switch backends without re-instrumenting my code

citations.quote: If your application is already instrumented with OpenTelemetry, you can send OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) data directly to Honeycomb.
Honeycomb supports receiving telemetry data via OpenTelemetry’s native protocol, OTLP, over gRPC, HTTP/protobuf, and HTTP/JSON.
Instrument your applications with OpenTelemetry, the open-source standard for collecting telemetry, and send traces, logs, and metrics to Honeycomb.
otel-migration: How to migrate proprietary or legacy instrumentation to OpenTelemetry.
